speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with gait and limb ataxia; to help me narrow down the cause given your significant medical history, could you tell me exactly when these symptoms first started and if they are progressive?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like acute cerebellar dysfunction; is the ataxia on the right side worsening steadily, and do you have any history of stroke, multiple sclerosis, or recent head trauma? Also, have you experienced any sudden onset of severe headache, vertigo, or difficulty speaking?

REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain (Cerebellum and Brainstem)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). The MRI confirms multifocal demyelinating lesions in the cerebellum and brainstem consistent with PML, likely secondary to an underlying immunocompromised state. I recommend immediate evaluation for HIV, lymphoma, or other causes of immune suppression.
